name: Vietnam
visual_anchor: Cinematic vertical 9:16 view of Ha Long Bay emerald waters with limestone karsts shrouded in morning mist.
core_traits: S-shaped coastline along Indochinese peninsula
Capital city is Hanoi, largest city is Ho Chi Minh City
World-renowned for Pho and Banh Mi
Traditional conical hat (Non La) and Ao Dai

facts_and_myths.claim: Vietnam is the world's largest exporter of Robusta coffee.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Vietnam produces and exports more Robusta coffee beans than any other country in the world.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Egg coffee (Ca phe trung) originated in Hanoi in the 1940s.

facts_and_myths.claim: Son Doong in Vietnam is the largest natural cave in the world.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Discovered by a local farmer and explored by BCRA, it has cavern sections large enough to house a 40-story skyscraper.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It even possesses its own localized weather and cloud system.

facts_and_myths.claim: Pho was originally an ancient dish eaten during the Hung Kings era.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Pho actually originated in the late 19th or early 20th century in northern Vietnam, heavily influenced by French-era culinary trade.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Nam Dinh and Hanoi are widely celebrated as the dual cradles of authentic Pho.

name: Japan
visual_anchor: Mount Fuji capped with snow framed by blooming pink sakura cherry blossoms and a red pagoda.
core_traits: Island nation shaped like an archipelago in East Asia
Capital is Tokyo, the world's most populous metropolitan area
Birthplace of Anime, Manga, and Shinkansen bullet trains
Famous culinary culture centered on Sushi and Ramen

facts_and_myths.claim: Mount Fuji is an active volcano.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Mount Fuji is classified as an active stratovolcano, though its last major eruption was in 1707.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It stands at 3,776 meters tall.

facts_and_myths.claim: Fortune cookies were invented in ancient Japan.
facts_and_myths.explanation: While a similar sesame cracker existed in Kyoto, the modern sweet fortune cookie was created by Japanese immigrants in California in the early 20th century.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In China, fortune cookies are virtually unknown except as American novelties.

name: France
visual_anchor: Glowing Eiffel Tower towering over the Seine River in Paris at twilight with vintage cobblestone streets.
core_traits: Hexagonal territory located in Western Europe
Capital is Paris, known as the City of Light
Global epicenter of haute cuisine, wine, cheese, and fashion
Home to the Louvre Museum and Mona Lisa

facts_and_myths.claim: France is the most visited country by international tourists in the world.
facts_and_myths.explanation: France routinely welcomes over 85 to 90 million international tourist arrivals annually.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: There are over 1,200 distinct varieties of French cheese produced nationwide.

facts_and_myths.claim: Croissants were originally invented by French bakers in Paris.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The precursor to the croissant is the Austrian Kipferl, which originated in Vienna and was later popularized in France.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Marie Antoinette is often said to have popularized Austrian pastries in Versailles.

name: United States
visual_anchor: Majestic Statue of Liberty against the Manhattan skyscraper skyline under fiery sunset clouds.
core_traits: Spans 50 states across North America from Atlantic to Pacific
Federal capital is Washington D.C., financial hub is New York City
Birthplace of Hollywood, NASA Apollo missions, and the internet
Famous symbols include the Bald Eagle and Stars & Stripes flag

facts_and_myths.claim: The United States has no official federal language declared by law.
facts_and_myths.explanation: While English is the de facto national language, the US federal government has never codified an official language by federal statute.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Dozens of individual states have designated English as their official state language.

facts_and_myths.claim: George Washington had dentures made of wood.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Washington's dentures were actually crafted from hippopotamus ivory, gold, brass screws, and human teeth, not wood.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Over time, wine and tea stained the ivory to look like wood grain.

name: United Kingdom
visual_anchor: Big Ben clock tower and the Houses of Parliament beside a red double-decker bus on Westminster Bridge.
core_traits: Island nation consisting of England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland
Capital is London, divided by the River Thames
Famous for afternoon tea, the Monarchy, and William Shakespeare
Iconic red telephone booths and double-decker buses

facts_and_myths.claim: Big Ben is the name of the clock tower itself.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The tower is officially named Elizabeth Tower; Big Ben is the nickname of the giant 13-ton bell inside.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The tower was formerly known simply as the Clock Tower before 2012.

facts_and_myths.claim: Buckingham Palace is the official London residence of the reigning monarch.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It has served as the official administrative headquarters of the British monarch since 1837.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The palace contains 775 rooms, including 78 bathrooms.

name: Italy
visual_anchor: Ancient Colosseum in Rome bathed in warm afternoon sunlight with Italian cypress trees.
core_traits: Distinctive boot-shaped peninsula jutting into the Mediterranean
Capital is Rome, cradling the Vatican City enclave
Cradle of the Roman Empire and the Renaissance
Famous gastronomy includes Pasta, Pizza, and Gelato

facts_and_myths.claim: Tomatoes have been an integral part of Italian cuisine since ancient Roman times.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Tomatoes are native to the Americas and did not reach Italy until the 16th century following the Columbian Exchange.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Italians initially regarded tomatoes with suspicion, suspecting them to be poisonous.

facts_and_myths.claim: Italy contains more UNESCO World Heritage sites than any other nation.
facts_and_myths.explanation: With 59 official World Heritage sites, Italy ties with or leads the global ranking.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Venice and its lagoon are listed as an entire collective heritage site.

name: China
visual_anchor: The Great Wall of China snaking endlessly over steep mist-covered green mountain ridges.
core_traits: Vast territory in East Asia with thousands of years of dynastic history
Capital is Beijing, economic megalopolis is Shanghai
Inventions include paper, printing, gunpowder, and the compass
Native habitat of the Giant Panda

facts_and_myths.claim: The Great Wall of China is visible from low Earth orbit with the naked eye.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Astronauts confirm the wall is too narrow and blends into the surrounding landscape, making it invisible without magnification.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Highways and airport runways are far more visible from orbit than the Great Wall.

facts_and_myths.claim: Giant Pandas are strictly native to central and southwestern China.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Wild giant pandas live exclusively in a few mountain ranges in Sichuan, Shaanxi, and Gansu provinces.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: All pandas lent to foreign zoos remain the diplomatic property of China.

name: South Korea
visual_anchor: Futuristic Seoul skyline featuring N Seoul Tower overlooking illuminated ancient Gyeongbokgung Palace at dusk.
core_traits: Peninsular nation in East Asia bordered to the north by the DMZ
Capital is Seoul, one of the world's most high-tech smart cities
Global cultural wave known as Hallyu (K-Pop, K-Dramas)
Signature culinary staple is Kimchi

facts_and_myths.claim: South Korea is the global pioneer in commercial 5G network rollout.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In April 2019, South Korea became the first country in the world to launch nationwide commercial 5G services.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In South Korea, infants were traditionally considered one year old on the day of their birth.

facts_and_myths.claim: Sleeping in an enclosed room with an electric fan running will cause fatal suffocation.
facts_and_myths.explanation: This is a widespread Korean urban legend known as 'fan death'; electric fans cannot consume oxygen or induce hypothermia in normal rooms.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Many fans sold in Korea still come equipped with auto-shutoff timers.

name: Germany
visual_anchor: Fairy-tale Neuschwanstein Castle nestled in Bavarian alpine pine forests under morning sun.
core_traits: Economic powerhouse located in Central Europe
Capital is Berlin, known for the Brandenburg Gate and historic wall
Famous for precision engineering, Autobahn highways, and automotive brands
Host of the world-renowned annual Oktoberfest beer festival

facts_and_myths.claim: Parts of the German Autobahn highway system have no federal speed limit.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Over half of the Autobahn network operates with an advisory speed recommendation (130 km/h) rather than a strict legal speed limit.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Running out of fuel on the Autobahn is considered illegal negligence.

facts_and_myths.claim: Oktoberfest takes place entirely during the month of October.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Most of Oktoberfest occurs during the final two weeks of September and concludes on the first weekend of October.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It was founded in 1810 to celebrate a royal Bavarian wedding.

name: Egypt
visual_anchor: Great Pyramid of Giza and the Sphinx standing timelessly amidst golden desert sands under glowing desert sun.
core_traits: Transcontinental country linking northeast Africa with the Middle East
Capital is Cairo, sliced through by the historic River Nile
Ancient civilization famous for Pharaohs, Mummies, and Hieroglyphs
Vital maritime chokepoint Suez Canal

facts_and_myths.claim: Cleopatra was of native Egyptian ethnic heritage.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Cleopatra VII was of Macedonian Greek ancestry, descending from Ptolemy I Soter, one of Alexander the Great's generals.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: She was, however, the first Ptolemaic ruler to learn to speak Egyptian.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Nile River is historically recognized as the longest river on Earth.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Stretching roughly 6,650 kilometers northward into the Mediterranean, it is widely considered the longest river system.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Nile flows south to north, opposite to most major world rivers.

name: Brazil
visual_anchor: Christ the Redeemer statue with open arms overlooking Guanabara Bay and Sugarloaf Mountain in Rio de Janeiro.
core_traits: Largest country in South America by both land and population
Capital is Brasilia, most famous cultural city is Rio de Janeiro
Home to the vast majority of the Amazon Rainforest and River
Celebrated for Samba, Rio Carnival, and five FIFA World Cup trophies

facts_and_myths.claim: Rio de Janeiro is the official political capital of Brazil.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Brasilia has been the planned federal capital since 1960; Rio de Janeiro was the capital before that.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Brasilia's master urban layout is shaped like an airplane from above.

facts_and_myths.claim: Brazil has won more men's FIFA World Cup championships than any other nation.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Brazil holds five titles (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, and 2002).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Pele is the only player to have won three World Cups.

name: Australia
visual_anchor: Sydney Opera House iconic shell sails glowing in Sydney Harbour with the Harbour Bridge in the backdrop.
core_traits: Both a continent and an island nation surrounded by oceans
Capital is Canberra, while Sydney and Melbourne are largest
Home to the Great Barrier Reef and the Outback red monolith Uluru
Unique endemic marsupials like Kangaroos and Koalas

facts_and_myths.claim: Sydney is the capital city of Australia.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Canberra was chosen as a compromise compromise capital in 1908 to resolve the fierce rivalry between Sydney and Melbourne.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Canberra means 'meeting place' in the local Ngunnawal language.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Great Barrier Reef is the largest living organism structure on Earth.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Composed of billions of tiny coral polyps, it covers over 344,000 square kilometers and is visible from space.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It hosts more than 1,500 species of fish.

name: India
visual_anchor: Taj Mahal white marble dome reflecting symmetrically in the tranquil reflecting pool at sunrise.
core_traits: Giant subcontinent in South Asia bounded by the Indian Ocean
Capital is New Delhi, financial center is Mumbai
Birthplace of Hinduism, Buddhism, Yoga, and Ayurvedic medicine
Famous for rich aromatic curries, spices, and Bollywood cinema

facts_and_myths.claim: India is officially the most populous country in the world.
facts_and_myths.explanation: UN population demographic data confirmed India surpassed China in total population in 2023.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: India has over 22 officially recognized languages.

facts_and_myths.claim: Chess was originally invented in ancient Europe.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Chess originated in northern India around the 6th century CE as a strategy game named Chaturanga.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Chaturanga modeled four military divisions: infantry, cavalry, elephants, and chariots.

name: Russia
visual_anchor: Saint Basil's Cathedral vibrant candy-colored onion domes in Red Square Moscow under swirling snowflakes.
core_traits: Largest country in the world by landmass spanning 11 time zones
Capital is Moscow, cultural window to Europe is Saint Petersburg
Famous for the Trans-Siberian Railway, Ballet, and Matryoshka nesting dolls
Spans across both Eastern Europe and northern Asia (Siberia)

facts_and_myths.claim: Lake Baikal in Russia contains about 20% of the world's unfrozen freshwater.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is both the deepest and oldest freshwater lake on Earth, holding more water than all North American Great Lakes combined.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The lake is home to the world's only exclusively freshwater seal, the Nerpa.

facts_and_myths.claim: Russia sold Alaska to the United States for billions of dollars.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In 1867, Russia sold Alaska for just 7.2 million US dollars (about 2 cents per acre at the time).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Critics initially mocked the deal as 'Seward's Folly' before gold and oil were found.

name: Canada
visual_anchor: Turquoise waters of Lake Louise in Banff surrounded by snow-dusted Canadian Rockies and lush evergreen trees.
core_traits: Second largest country by land area, occupying northern North America
Capital is Ottawa, largest metropolis is Toronto, French-speaking hub is Montreal
National symbols include the red Maple Leaf and the Beaver
Renowned for Ice Hockey, Maple Syrup, and immense boreal forests

facts_and_myths.claim: Canada has the longest national coastline in the world.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Canada's coastline measures over 202,080 kilometers bordering three oceans: Atlantic, Pacific, and Arctic.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Canada also contains more than 60% of all natural lakes on planet Earth.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Mounties (RCMP) conduct all daily police patrols on horseback.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Modern Royal Canadian Mounted Police use standard police cruisers and utility vehicles; horses are reserved for ceremonies.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The famous Musical Ride is their signature equestrian ceremony.

name: Spain
visual_anchor: Soaring organic towers of Sagrada Familia in Barcelona bathed in golden Catalan sunlight.
core_traits: Occupies the majority of the Iberian Peninsula in southwestern Europe
Capital is Madrid, Catalan jewel is Barcelona
Birthplace of Flamenco dancing, Paella, and Tapas culture
World-famous football giants Real Madrid and FC Barcelona

facts_and_myths.claim: The Sagrada Familia basilica has taken longer to construct than the Egyptian pyramids.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Construction began in 1882 under Antoni Gaudi and is still ongoing over 140 years later.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The project relies entirely on private donations and ticket revenues.

facts_and_myths.claim: Bulls become enraged specifically by the color red.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Bulls are dichromatic and cannot distinguish red; they react aggressively to the rapid waving motion of the matador's cape.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A blue or white cape waved aggressively evokes the exact same charging reaction.

name: Mexico
visual_anchor: El Castillo pyramid at Chichen Itza standing boldly against a sapphire tropical sky.
core_traits: Located in southern North America bordering the US to the north
Capital is Mexico City, built on the historic ruins of Aztec Tenochtitlan
Famous for Tacos, Guacamole, Tequila, and Mariachi music
Celebrates the colorful Day of the Dead (Dia de los Muertos)

facts_and_myths.claim: Cinco de Mayo is Mexico's official Independence Day.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Cinco de Mayo commemorates the 1862 Battle of Puebla against the French; Mexico's actual Independence Day is September 16.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Cinco de Mayo is celebrated much more widely in the United States than in Mexico.

facts_and_myths.claim: Chocolate originated from ancient Mesoamerican civilizations in Mexico.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Olmecs, Mayans, and Aztecs brewed ground cacao beans into a sacred bitter frothy beverage.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Aztecs used cacao beans as official currency.

name: Thailand
visual_anchor: Gilded spires of the Grand Palace and Wat Arun temple reflecting on the Chao Phraya River in Bangkok.
core_traits: Located at the center of the Indochinese peninsula in Southeast Asia
Capital is Bangkok (Krung Thep), famous for vibrant floating markets
Famed for Tom Yum soup, Pad Thai, and Mango Sticky Rice
National combat martial art is Muay Thai

facts_and_myths.claim: Thailand is the only Southeast Asian nation never colonized by a European power.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Through skilled diplomacy and modernization by King Chulalongkorn, Siam remained an independent buffer state.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Bangkok's ceremonial name is recognized as the longest place name in the world (168 letters).

facts_and_myths.claim: Red Bull energy drink was originally invented in Austria.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It originated in Thailand as 'Krating Daeng' before Austrian entrepreneur Dietrich Mateschitz partnered to market it globally.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Krating Daeng literally translates to 'Red Gaur' (a wild Asian bovine).

name: Greece
visual_anchor: Parthenon temple on the rocky Acropolis hill overlooking Athens under golden Mediterranean daylight.
core_traits: Southern European nation comprising thousands of Aegean and Ionian islands
Capital is Athens, one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities
Cradle of Western civilization, Democracy, and the Olympic Games
Famous for Greek salad, Feta cheese, and Olive groves

facts_and_myths.claim: The first modern Olympic Games were revived in Athens in 1896.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Honoring its ancient roots dating back to 776 BC in Olympia, Athens hosted the inaugural modern Olympiad.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Winners in 1896 received silver medals and olive branches, not gold.

facts_and_myths.claim: Ancient Greek marble statues and temples were always pristine gleaming white.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Original classical Greek statues and friezes were vividly painted with bright, gaudy colors that wore off over millennia.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Ultraviolet light analysis reveals traces of vibrant red, gold, and blue pigments on relics.

name: Switzerland
visual_anchor: Sharp pyramid summit of the Matterhorn mountain looming over alpine meadows and wooden chalets.
core_traits: Landlocked mountainous country in Central Europe dominated by the Alps
Federal city is Bern, banking and international hubs are Zurich and Geneva
Renowned for Swiss watches, pocket knives, and luxury chocolate
Longstanding international armed neutrality

facts_and_myths.claim: Geneva is the political capital city of Switzerland.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Bern is the de facto federal seat of government (Federal City); Switzerland technically has no single de jure constitutional capital.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Switzerland possesses four official languages: German, French, Italian, and Romansh.

facts_and_myths.claim: Switzerland has enough nuclear bomb fallout shelter space for its entire population.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Swiss federal law requires every citizen to have a designated shelter space in their building or community bunker.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Sonnenberg Tunnel was once equipped to shelter 20,000 people.

name: Netherlands
visual_anchor: Traditional wooden windmills alongside a vibrant striped tulip field and quiet canal.
core_traits: Low-lying country in Western Europe where much land sits below sea level
Constitutional capital is Amsterdam, seat of government is The Hague
Famed for bicycles, canals, tulips, and Gouda cheese
Engineering masters of dikes, dams, and land reclamation (polders)

facts_and_myths.claim: Holland is the official country name for the entire Netherlands nation.
facts_and_myths.explanation: North and South Holland are merely two of the country's twelve administrative provinces.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Dutch government officially dropped the brand name 'Holland' in 2020.

facts_and_myths.claim: There are more bicycles in the Netherlands than human residents.
facts_and_myths.explanation: With around 18 million people, there are an estimated 23 million bicycles in active circulation.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Utrecht houses the world's largest underground bike parking garage for 12,500 bikes.

name: Singapore
visual_anchor: Futuristic Supertree Grove at Gardens by the Bay with Marina Bay Sands glowing against the night sky.
core_traits: Island city-state located at the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula
Capital and nation are the same single global metropolitan city
Iconic national symbol is the Merlion (half lion, half fish)
World-leading financial hub with world's busiest container transshipment port

facts_and_myths.claim: Singapore is one of only three surviving sovereign city-states in the modern world.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The other two sovereign city-states are Monaco and Vatican City.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Singapore has expanded its physical land area by over 25% through land reclamation.

facts_and_myths.claim: Chewing gum is completely banned in Singapore under all circumstances.
facts_and_myths.explanation: While the sale and import of standard chewing gum is prohibited, therapeutic and dental gum prescribed by doctors is legal.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The ban was introduced in 1992 to stop vandals from jamming MRT train doors.

name: Argentina
visual_anchor: Thunderous cascading curtain of Iguazu Falls surrounded by lush subtropical rainforest mist.
core_traits: Stretches along southern South America between the Andes and the Atlantic
Capital is Buenos Aires, nicknamed the Paris of South America
Birthplace of the Tango dance and football icons Maradona and Messi
Renowned for premium beef, Asado barbecues, and Patagonia glaciers

facts_and_myths.claim: Argentina is named after the precious metal silver.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The name derives from the Latin 'argentum' (silver), linked to the legend of the Sierra de la Plata mountains.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Spanish explorers named the Rio de la Plata 'River of Silver'.

facts_and_myths.claim: Tango dance originated in upscale European ballrooms.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Tango originated in the working-class port brothels and tenements of Buenos Aires and Montevideo in the late 19th century.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It blended African rhythms, Cuban habanera, and European polkas.

name: Turkey
visual_anchor: Hundreds of colorful hot air balloons floating over the fairy chimneys of Cappadocia at dawn.
core_traits: Transcontinental bridge connecting Southeastern Europe and Western Asia
Capital is Ankara, largest historic metropolis is Istanbul
Home to the historic Hagia Sophia and Grand Bazaar
Famous for Turkish coffee, Baklava, and Turkish delight

facts_and_myths.claim: Istanbul is the political capital of Turkey.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Mustafa Kemal Ataturk moved the capital to Ankara in central Anatolia in 1923.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Istanbul was formerly known as Byzantium and Constantinople.

facts_and_myths.claim: Istanbul is the only metropolis in the world situated across two continents.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Bosphorus Strait bisects Istanbul into European and Asian halves.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Commuters cross continents daily in 15 minutes by ferry or undersea metro.

name: South Africa
visual_anchor: Flat-topped Table Mountain rising dramatically behind the coastal harbor of Cape Town.
core_traits: Located at the southernmost tip of the African continent
Has three separate capital cities: Pretoria, Cape Town, and Bloemfontein
Homeland of Nelson Mandela and host of the 2010 FIFA World Cup
Famous for Kruger National Park and the Big Five safari animals

facts_and_myths.claim: South Africa has three distinct official capital cities.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Pretoria is executive, Cape Town is legislative, and Bloemfontein is judicial.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The country recognizes 12 official languages including South African Sign Language.

facts_and_myths.claim: Johannesburg was founded as an ancient tribal citadel.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Johannesburg was founded as a wild gold rush boomtown in 1886 following the discovery of the Witwatersrand gold reef.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It is one of the very few major global cities not built on a coast, lake, or major river.

name: Saudi Arabia
visual_anchor: Endless golden dunes of the Rub' al Khali Empty Quarter desert stretching to the glowing horizon.
core_traits: Dominates the vast majority of the Arabian Peninsula in the Middle East
Capital is Riyadh, historic Red Sea port is Jeddah
Cradle of Islam containing Mecca and Medina, the two holiest cities
World's leading petroleum exporter possessing massive oil reserves

facts_and_myths.claim: Saudi Arabia has no permanent natural rivers flowing through its borders.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It is the largest country in the world by area without a single permanent flowing river.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Water needs are supplied by deep groundwater aquifers and colossal seawater desalination plants.

facts_and_myths.claim: Camels are native exclusively to the Arabian desert.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Early camel ancestors actually evolved in North America before migrating across the Bering land bridge to Asia and Africa.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Saudi Arabia today actually imports camels from Australia for meat and racing.

name: Norway
visual_anchor: Deep blue waters of Geirangerfjord framed by towering vertical cliffs and cascading waterfalls.
core_traits: Scandinavian nation occupying the western portion of the Scandinavian Peninsula
Capital is Oslo, gateway to Arctic Svalbard archipelago
Famous for dramatic glacial fjords and dancing Northern Lights (Aurora)
Viking heritage and world leader in electric vehicle adoption

facts_and_myths.claim: The sun does not set for months during summer in northern Norway.
facts_and_myths.explanation: North of the Arctic Circle, the midnight sun shines continuously from late May to late July.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Svalbard town of Longyearbyen experiences four months without sunset.

facts_and_myths.claim: Vikings wore helmets adorned with large animal horns into battle.
facts_and_myths.explanation: 19th-century romantic opera costume designers invented the horned helmet myth; real Viking helmets were smooth conical iron caps.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Horns would have been dangerous in combat because enemy swords and axes could hook onto them.

name: Sweden
visual_anchor: Gamla Stan historic pastel buildings clustered on Stockholm's waterfront canals under clear northern sky.
core_traits: Largest Scandinavian country by area and population
Capital is Stockholm, built across 14 islands connected by 57 bridges
Birthplace of the Nobel Prize, IKEA, Spotify, and pop legends ABBA
Famous for Fika coffee break culture and meatballs with lingonberry

facts_and_myths.claim: The Nobel Peace Prize is presented in Stockholm along with all other Nobel Prizes.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Alfred Nobel's will designated that the Peace Prize be awarded in Oslo, Norway, while the other prizes are awarded in Stockholm.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Alfred Nobel made his massive fortune by inventing dynamite.

facts_and_myths.claim: Sweden imports garbage from other countries to power its recycling energy plants.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Sweden's waste-to-energy incineration system is so efficient that it imports over 2 million tons of waste annually from neighbors.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Less than 1% of Swedish household waste ends up in landfills.

name: New Zealand
aliases: Land of the Long White Cloud
visual_anchor: Snowy Southern Alps reflecting in crystal Lake Wakatipu near Queenstown.
core_traits: Island country in the southwestern Pacific consisting of North and South Islands
Capital is Wellington, largest commercial center is Auckland
Indigenous Maori culture and the famous Haka ceremonial dance
Filming location of the legendary 'Lord of the Rings' cinematic trilogies

facts_and_myths.claim: New Zealand has more sheep than human beings.
facts_and_myths.explanation: With a human population of 5 million, New Zealand is home to approximately 25 million sheep (about 5 sheep per person).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In the 1980s, the ratio was over 20 sheep per person.

facts_and_myths.claim: Auckland is the constitutional capital of New Zealand.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Wellington replaced Auckland as the capital in 1865 due to its central geographical position.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Wellington is the world's southernmost sovereign capital city.

name: Indonesia
visual_anchor: Ancient stone stupas of Borobudur temple silhouetted against sunrise with Mount Merapi in the background.
core_traits: World's largest archipelagic state spanning over 17,000 tropical islands
Capital is Jakarta (transitioning to planned forest capital Nusantara)
Home to Komodo dragons and lush tropical volcanic landscapes like Bali
Most populous Muslim-majority nation on Earth

facts_and_myths.claim: The Komodo dragon is the largest living lizard on Earth.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Native to five Indonesian islands, these predatory monitor lizards can exceed 3 meters in length and 70 kilograms in weight.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Their saliva delivers toxic proteins that prevent prey's blood from clotting.

facts_and_myths.claim: Bali is an independent sovereign island country.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Bali is one of the 38 provinces of the Republic of Indonesia.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Bali maintains a unique Balinese Hindu culture distinct from the Muslim-majority rest of the nation.

name: Cuba
visual_anchor: Vintage 1950s colorful classic American cars cruising past colonial pastel facades along Havana's Malecon sea drive.
core_traits: Largest island nation in the Caribbean Sea located south of Florida
Capital is Havana, famous for historic colonial plazas and fortresses
Famed for Cuban cigars, Havana Club rum, and lively Salsa rhythm
Signature historical figures include Che Guevara and Fidel Castro

facts_and_myths.claim: Cuba has one of the highest doctor-to-patient ratios in the world.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Cuba's comprehensive medical system trains vast numbers of physicians and dispatches medical brigades globally.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Cuba developed its own homegrown COVID-19 vaccines (Abdala and Soberana).

facts_and_myths.claim: The Cuba Libre cocktail was created to celebrate the Cuban socialist revolution of 1959.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It originated around 1900 during the Spanish-American War when US soldiers mixed Coca-Cola with local rum and lime.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The toast 'Por Cuba Libre' meant 'To a Free Cuba' from Spanish colonial rule.

name: Peru
visual_anchor: Spectacular stone citadel ruins of Machu Picchu perched high on a lush Andean ridge enveloped in mist.
core_traits: Western South American country facing the South Pacific Ocean
Capital is Lima, historic Inca imperial capital is Cusco
Heartland of the ancient Inca Empire and enigmatic Nazca Lines
Culinary capital celebrated for Ceviche and over 3,000 potato varieties

facts_and_myths.claim: Potatoes were first cultivated in the Andean highlands of Peru.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Indigenous Andean peoples domesticated wild potatoes near Lake Titicaca over 7,000 years ago.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Peru preserves over 3,000 native varieties in every color and texture.

facts_and_myths.claim: Machu Picchu was lost because the Spanish conquistadors razed it to the ground.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Spanish conquistadors never found Machu Picchu; it was abandoned and preserved intact until Hiram Bingham brought it to global attention in 1911.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The stone blocks fit together so precisely without mortar that a knife blade cannot slip between them.

name: Portugal
visual_anchor: Vintage yellow Tram 28 climbing the steep narrow cobblestone hills of Alfama in Lisbon.
core_traits: Located on the Atlantic coast of the Iberian Peninsula next to Spain
Capital is Lisbon, northern historic wine city is Porto
Pioneered the Age of Discovery with navigators like Vasco da Gama
Famous for Pastel de Nata custard tarts and Port wine

facts_and_myths.claim: Lisbon is older than Rome.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Lisbon was settled by the Phoenicians around 1200 BC, making it four centuries older than Rome.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Half of the world's commercial cork production originates from Portuguese cork oak forests.

facts_and_myths.claim: Portugal and Spain share the exact same official language.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Portuguese is a distinct Romance language with unique phonology, grammar, and vocabulary.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Portuguese is spoken by over 250 million people worldwide across four continents.

name: Belgium
visual_anchor: Gilded baroque guildhalls lining the cobblestone Grand Place square in Brussels at dusk.
core_traits: Western European nation bordered by France, Germany, and the Netherlands
Capital is Brussels, headquarters of both the European Union and NATO
Famous for Belgian waffles, luxury pralines chocolate, and Trappist beers
Home to classic comic heroes Tintin and The Smurfs

facts_and_myths.claim: French fries were originally invented in Belgium, not France.
facts_and_myths.explanation: River villagers in the Meuse Valley fried potatoes when winter froze rivers; American soldiers misnamed them 'French fries' because the Belgian army spoke French.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Belgium has dedicated French fry museums (Frietmuseum).

facts_and_myths.claim: Belgium has only one unified national language.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Belgium has three official languages: Dutch (Flemish), French, and German.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The country is divided into distinct linguistic and political communities.

name: Ireland
visual_anchor: Sheer vertical drop of the Cliffs of Moher plunging into the wild frothy Atlantic Ocean.
core_traits: Island nation in the North Atlantic known for lush green countryside
Capital is Dublin, birthplace of Guinness stout and James Joyce
Famous cultural symbols include the Shamrock clover, Celtic harp, and Leprechauns
Celebrates Saint Patrick's Day worldwide every March 17

facts_and_myths.claim: Saint Patrick banished all snakes from the island of Ireland.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Ireland never had native snakes post-Ice Age; 'snakes' was a religious metaphor for pagan practices.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Celtic harp is Ireland's official national emblem, making it the only nation with a musical instrument as its state symbol.

facts_and_myths.claim: Halloween originated from an ancient Celtic festival in Ireland.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The modern holiday evolved directly from Samhain, an ancient Gaelic harvest festival marking the start of winter.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Original jack-o'-lanterns were carved from turnips, not pumpkins.

name: Iceland
visual_anchor: Steamy milky-blue thermal waters of the Blue Lagoon surrounded by black volcanic lava rocks.
core_traits: Nordic island nation situated in the North Atlantic on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge
Capital is Reykjavik, the northernmost sovereign capital in the world
Known for active volcanoes, massive glaciers, geysers, and geothermal spas
100% powered by renewable geothermal and hydroelectric energy

facts_and_myths.claim: Iceland has no native wild mosquitoes anywhere in the country.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Due to unpredictable temperature swings that interrupt mosquito life cycles, Iceland is virtually mosquito-free.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Iceland also has no operational public railway system.

facts_and_myths.claim: Iceland is completely covered in ice while Greenland is lush green.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Only about 11% of Iceland is covered by glaciers; Greenland is over 80% covered by a permanent ice sheet.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Viking legend says Erik the Red named Greenland to attract gullible settlers.

name: Denmark
visual_anchor: Colorful 17th-century merchant townhouses lining the vibrant canal harbor of Nyhavn in Copenhagen.
core_traits: Scandinavian nation comprising the Jutland peninsula and hundreds of Baltic islands
Capital is Copenhagen, home to the Little Mermaid statue and Tivoli Gardens
Birthplace of Lego building bricks and fairy tale writer Hans Christian Andersen
Famous for the cozy cultural philosophy of Hygge

facts_and_myths.claim: Lego bricks were invented and first manufactured in Denmark.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Carpenter Ole Kirk Christiansen created Lego in the Danish town of Billund in 1932.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The name Lego comes from the Danish words 'leg godt', meaning 'play well'.

facts_and_myths.claim: Denmark has rugged high alpine mountain ranges.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Denmark is extremely flat; its highest natural elevation point, Mollehoj, is only 171 meters above sea level.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Greenland is an autonomous territory within the Realm of Denmark.

name: Finland
visual_anchor: Snowy pine forest in Lapland with wooden sauna cabin glowing warmly under green Aurora lights.
core_traits: Northern European Nordic country bordered by Sweden, Norway, and Russia
Capital is Helsinki on the Gulf of Finland
Known for traditional wood-fired saunas, Nokia telecommunications, and Angry Birds
Official mythical home of Santa Claus in Rovaniemi, Lapland

facts_and_myths.claim: There are more saunas in Finland than passenger cars.
facts_and_myths.explanation: With 5.5 million people, Finland boasts over 3 million saunas (even in parliament and apartment buildings).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Sauna is the only Finnish word adopted into standard English.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Finnish language belongs to the Scandinavian Germanic language family.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Finnish is Finno-Ugric, closely related to Estonian and Hungarian, completely distinct from Swedish or Norwegian.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Finland consistently ranks #1 as the happiest country in the world in UN reports.

name: Austria
visual_anchor: Grand Schonbrunn Palace imperial gardens in Vienna glowing in warm baroque splendor.
core_traits: Landlocked mountainous nation in Central Europe dominated by the Eastern Alps
Capital is Vienna, famed for classical music, imperial palaces, and grand cafes
Homeland of classical composers Mozart, Haydn, and Schubert
Famous for Wiener Schnitzel, Sachertorte chocolate cake, and alpine skiing

facts_and_myths.claim: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was born in Vienna.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Mozart was born in the city of Salzburg (which was then part of the Prince-Archbishopric of Salzburg).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Vienna is where Mozart lived, composed his greatest operas, and died.

facts_and_myths.claim: Vienna has the oldest operating public zoo in the world.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Tiergarten Schonbrunn was founded as an imperial menagerie in 1752 and remains open today.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It was one of the few European zoos to naturally breed giant pandas.

name: Poland
visual_anchor: Restored brick gothic Royal Castle and pastel Old Town marketplace square in Warsaw.
core_traits: Central European country along the Baltic Sea with a resilient historic heritage
Capital is Warsaw, historic royal cultural capital is Krakow
Homeland of astronomer Nicolaus Copernicus, Marie Curie, and composer Chopin
Traditional dishes include Pierogi dumplings and Kielbasa sausage

facts_and_myths.claim: Marie Curie was born and raised in France.
facts_and_myths.explanation: She was born Maria Sklodowska in Warsaw, Poland; she later moved to Paris to pursue university education.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: She named the chemical element Polonium in honor of her native homeland Poland.

facts_and_myths.claim: Poland is home to the world's largest brick castle by land area.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Malbork Castle, built by Teutonic Knights in the 13th century, is the largest brick castle complex on Earth.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Bialowieza Forest in Poland is home to the largest wild European bison population.

name: Philippines
visual_anchor: Lush green conical formations of the Chocolate Hills in Bohol under tropical sunshine.
core_traits: Archipelago of over 7,000 tropical islands in Southeast Asia
Capital is Manila, famous for colorful Jeepneys and bustling harbors
Famous for natural wonders like Boracay white beaches and Chocolate Hills
Passion for basketball, singing karaoke, and national dish Adobo

facts_and_myths.claim: The Chocolate Hills in Bohol are made of chocolate-colored cocoa soil.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They are grass-covered limestone karst hills that turn chocolate-brown during the dry season.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: There are at least 1,260 individual hills in the formation.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Philippines is named after a Spanish monarch.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Spanish explorer Ruy Lopez de Villalobos named the islands Las Islas Filipinas in honor of King Philip II of Spain.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Philippines was under Spanish colonial rule for over 300 years.

name: Malaysia
visual_anchor: Illuminated metallic twin spires of the Petronas Towers soaring into the night sky of Kuala Lumpur.
core_traits: Southeast Asian nation split into Peninsular Malaysia and Malaysian Borneo
Federal capital is Kuala Lumpur, administrative hub is Putrajaya
Iconic landmarks include the Petronas Twin Towers and Batu Caves
Multicultural melting pot famous for Nasi Lemak and Roti Canai

facts_and_myths.claim: The Petronas Towers were once the tallest buildings in the world.
facts_and_myths.explanation: From 1998 to 2004, they held the official title of the world's tallest buildings and remain the tallest twin towers.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Tower 1 was built by a Japanese consortium while Tower 2 was built by a South Korean team in a race.

facts_and_myths.claim: Borneo island belongs entirely to Malaysia.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Borneo is shared among three nations: Indonesia (73%), Malaysia (26%), and Brunei (1%).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Borneo's rainforest is estimated to be 130 million years old, twice as old as the Amazon.

name: Morocco
visual_anchor: Vibrant blue painted walls and narrow cobbled alleys of Chefchaouen nestled against the Rif mountains.
core_traits: North African country bordering both the Atlantic Ocean and Mediterranean Sea
Capital is Rabat, largest economic metropolis is Casablanca, tourist gem is Marrakech
Famous for labyrinthine Medina bazaars, Tagine stews, and mint tea
Iconic blue pearl town of Chefchaouen

facts_and_myths.claim: Casablanca was primarily filmed on location on the streets of Morocco.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Almost the entire Hollywood film 'Casablanca' was shot inside Warner Bros. soundstages in Burbank, California.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Rick's Cafe was later constructed in real-life Casablanca to satisfy visiting movie tourists.

facts_and_myths.claim: Morocco is home to the oldest existing, continually operating university in the world.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez was founded by Fatima al-Fihri in 859 CE.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: UNESCO and Guinness World Records both recognize it as the oldest university.

name: Kenya
visual_anchor: Silhouetted acacia tree on the golden Maasai Mara savannah with Mount Kilimanjaro in the far haze.
core_traits: East African nation straddling the equator along the Indian Ocean
Capital is Nairobi, known as the Safari Capital of the World
Famed for the Maasai Mara Great Migration of millions of wildebeests
Global athletic powerhouse in middle and long-distance marathon running

facts_and_myths.claim: Mount Kilimanjaro is located inside Kenya.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Kilimanjaro is located in neighboring Tanzania, though the best panoramic views of its snow peaks are from Kenya's Amboseli Park.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Kenya's own Mount Kenya is the second-highest peak in Africa at 5,199 meters.

facts_and_myths.claim: Kenyan runners from the Kalenjin tribe dominate global marathon records.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Athletes from this region, such as Eliud Kipchoge, hold dozens of Olympic and world distance records.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: High altitude training in the Great Rift Valley enhances red blood cell oxygen capacity.

name: Chile
visual_anchor: Dramatic granite horn peaks of Torres del Paine rising above turquoise glacial lakes in Patagonia.
core_traits: Unusually long and narrow country squeezed between the Andes mountains and Pacific Ocean
Capital is Santiago, backed by snow-capped Andean ridges
Home to the driest non-polar desert on Earth, the Atacama Desert
Administers remote Easter Island (Rapa Nui) and its Moai statues

facts_and_myths.claim: The Atacama Desert in Chile has spots where rain has never been recorded in history.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Parts of the central Atacama have zero recorded rainfall across centuries, making it the driest place outside Antarctica.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: NASA uses the Atacama to test Mars rover exploration equipment.

facts_and_myths.claim: Easter Island is located just a few miles off the coast of mainland Chile.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Easter Island lies over 3,700 kilometers west of the Chilean coast in the middle of the Pacific Ocean.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It is one of the most geographically isolated inhabited islands on Earth.

name: Colombia
visual_anchor: Verdant Cocora Valley dotted with towering wax palm trees reaching into the highland clouds.
core_traits: Located in northwestern South America connecting Central and South America
Capital is Bogota, located high in the Andes plateau
World-renowned for premium Arabica coffee beans and fine emeralds
Second most biodiverse country on Earth behind Brazil

facts_and_myths.claim: Colombia produces over 70% of the world's highest quality emeralds.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Muzo and Chivor mines in Colombia are renowned for pure deep-green emerald gemstones.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Colombia's Quindio wax palms are the tallest palm trees in the world, reaching 60 meters.

facts_and_myths.claim: The country's name is spelled Columbia in English.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The correct name of the South American nation is Colombia (with an 'o'); Columbia (with a 'u') refers to US cities, rivers, or the university.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The national campaign 'It\'s Colombia, NOT Columbia' gained international fame.

name: Mongolia
aliases: Land of the Eternal Blue Sky
visual_anchor: Nomadic white felt yurt (Ger) standing on the boundless golden steppe beneath a vast azure sky.
core_traits: Vast landlocked country between Russia and China with low population density
Capital is Ulaanbaatar, the coldest sovereign capital city by average temperature
Homeland of Genghis Khan and the historic Mongol Empire
Nomadic horse-riding culture and the vast Gobi Desert

facts_and_myths.claim: Mongolia is the most sparsely populated sovereign country in the world.
facts_and_myths.explanation: With a territory three times the size of France and only 3.4 million people, it has roughly 2 people per square kilometer.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Horses outnumber humans in Mongolia.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Gobi Desert in Mongolia is covered completely in giant towering sand dunes.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Only about 3% of the Gobi consists of classic sand dunes; most of it is flat gravel plains, rocky ridges, and semi-arid steppe.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The world's first dinosaur egg fossils were discovered in the Gobi Desert in 1923.

name: Nepal
visual_anchor: Prayer flags fluttering in the icy mountain wind with the towering summit of Mount Everest behind them.
core_traits: Landlocked Himalayan nation nestled between India and China
Capital is Kathmandu, famous for historic Hindu and Buddhist temples
Home to 8 of the world's 10 tallest mountain peaks, including Everest
Only country in the world with a non-quadrilateral national flag

facts_and_myths.claim: Nepal's national flag is the only national flag in the world that is not a four-sided rectangle.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It consists of two stacked pennants representing the Himalayas and the two main religions, Hinduism and Buddhism.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The geometric mathematical construction of the flag is codified in Nepal's constitution.

facts_and_myths.claim: Mount Everest is entirely located inside the territory of Nepal.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The international border between Nepal and China (Tibet) runs directly across the highest summit point.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Everest is known as Sagarmatha in Nepali and Chomolungma in Tibetan.

name: Jamaica
visual_anchor: Turquoise Caribbean waters breaking onto white sand beach with lush green Blue Mountains in the distance.
core_traits: Caribbean island nation situated south of Cuba and west of Hispaniola
Capital is Kingston, situated on a large natural harbor
Birthplace of Reggae music and cultural icon Bob Marley
Dominant powerhouse in Olympic sprint athletics led by Usain Bolt

facts_and_myths.claim: Jamaica was the first Caribbean nation to gain independence in the 20th century.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Jamaica gained full independence from the United Kingdom in August 1962.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Jamaica's flag is the only national flag that does not contain red, white, or blue.

facts_and_myths.claim: Reggae music has existed in Jamaican culture for many centuries.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Reggae emerged recently in the late 1960s, evolving from earlier Jamaican styles like Ska and Rocksteady.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Bob Marley's 'One Love' was named song of the millennium by the BBC.

name: Vatican City
visual_anchor: Grand dome of Saint Peter's Basilica rising majestically over the elliptical colonnade of Saint Peter's Square.
core_traits: Completely landlocked microstate enclaved within the city of Rome, Italy
Smallest independent state in the world by both area and population
Spiritual and administrative headquarters of the Roman Catholic Church, ruled by the Pope
Contains Saint Peter's Basilica and the Sistine Chapel painted by Michelangelo

facts_and_myths.claim: Vatican City is the smallest sovereign nation on Earth in both land area and population.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It covers just 0.49 square kilometers (121 acres) and has a resident population under 800 people.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It has its own post office, telephone system, radio station, and euro coins.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Pope is guarded by an elite division of the Italian National Army.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Security is provided exclusively by the Pontifical Swiss Guard, founded in 1506.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Swiss Guards must be unmarried Swiss Catholic males who have completed Swiss military training.

name: Eiffel Tower
visual_anchor: Cinematic vertical 9:16 view of the illuminated wrought-iron lattice Eiffel Tower sparkling against the deep blue Parisian twilight sky above the Champ de Mars.
core_traits: Wrought-iron lattice tower located on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France
Engineered by Gustave Eiffel's company as the centerpiece of the 1889 World's Fair
Affectionately nicknamed 'The Iron Lady' (La Dame de Fer)
Stands approximately 330 meters tall and was the world's tallest man-made structure until 1930

facts_and_myths.claim: The Eiffel Tower grows taller during the hot summer months.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Thermal expansion of the puddle iron causes the tower to expand and rise up to 15 centimeters (6 inches) in summer heat.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It was originally slated for demolition after 20 years, but was preserved because it served as an invaluable telecommunications antenna.

facts_and_myths.claim: Gustave Eiffel was the original designer who drafted the tower's blueprints.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Senior structural engineers Maurice Koechlin and Emile Nouguier drafted the original plans, which Eiffel subsequently bought and championed.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Eiffel built a private rooftop apartment inside the tower where he famously entertained inventor Thomas Edison.

name: Great Wall of China
visual_anchor: Dramatic vertical 9:16 aerial shot of the serpentine stone fortifications of the Great Wall winding across misty mountain ridges under golden sunset light.
core_traits: Massive ancient fortification network snaking thousands of kilometers across northern China
Constructed and reinforced across multiple imperial dynasties, most prominently the Ming Dynasty
Features fortified watchtowers, beacon towers, garrison barracks, and battlements
Built to guard imperial borders against military incursions and nomadic invasions

facts_and_myths.claim: The Great Wall of China is easily visible from the Moon with the naked eye.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Astronauts and space agencies have repeatedly debunked this myth; the wall is too narrow and blends into natural rock formations to be seen unaided.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Sticky rice flour was incorporated into the mortar during the Ming Dynasty to give the brickwork astonishing seismic resilience.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Great Wall is one continuous, uninterrupted wall from end to end.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It comprises an extensive patchwork of walls, watchtowers, defensive trenches, and natural geographical ramparts like cliffs and rivers.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: When including all historical branches and trenches, the total network spans over 21,000 kilometers (13,000 miles).

name: Pyramids of Giza
visual_anchor: Sun-drenched vertical 9:16 cinematic panorama of the monumental limestone Giza Pyramids rising above golden desert dunes under a radiant azure sky.
core_traits: Monumental ancient burial complex located on the Giza Plateau on the western edge of Cairo, Egypt
Includes the Great Pyramid of Khufu, Khafre, and Menkaure alongside the Great Sphinx
Oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World and the only one still largely intact
Constructed over 4,500 years ago during the Fourth Dynasty of the Old Kingdom

facts_and_myths.claim: The Pyramids of Giza were built entirely by hundreds of thousands of enslaved laborers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Modern archaeological digs of the workers' village have proven that the builders were respected, well-fed Egyptian permanent and seasonal paid workers.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Great Pyramid of Khufu consists of approximately 2.3 million stone blocks weighing an average of 2.5 tons each.

facts_and_myths.claim: The pyramids originally gleamed brilliant white across the desert landscape.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They were originally encased in smooth, highly polished white Tura limestone that reflected the desert sunlight like mirrors before eroding over centuries.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Great Pyramid remained the tallest artificial structure on Earth for over 3,800 years until Lincoln Cathedral was built.

name: Colosseum
visual_anchor: Dramatic low-angle vertical 9:16 shot of the monumental multi-tiered travertine arches of the Roman Colosseum bathed in warm amber twilight.
core_traits: Massive freestanding oval amphitheater situated in the heart of Rome, Italy
Commissioned by Emperor Vespasian and completed under Titus around 80 AD
Famous for hosting gladiatorial combats, wild beast hunts, and public spectacles
Largest amphitheater ever constructed in antiquity, seating an estimated 50,000 to 80,000 spectators

facts_and_myths.claim: The Romans could flood the arena floor of the Colosseum to stage mock naval battles.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Historical chronicles record that water was channeled into the arena during inaugural games to stage realistic naval battles called naumachiae.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Colosseum featured a massive retractable canvas awning system called the velarium to shade spectators from blistering summer sun.

facts_and_myths.claim: Gladiatorial bouts always culminated in the ritual execution of the defeated fighter.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Gladiators were highly prized, expensive athletic investments; most fights ended upon submission or injury, with survival rates estimated at over 80%.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The name Colosseum derives from a colossal bronze statue of Emperor Nero that once stood just outside the amphitheater.

name: Taj Mahal
visual_anchor: Crisp symmetrical vertical 9:16 reflection of the ivory-white marble Taj Mahal mausoleum and four minarets in the glassy reflecting pool at misty sunrise.
core_traits: Monumental ivory-white marble mausoleum on the south bank of the Yamuna River in Agra, India
Commissioned in 1632 by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan to honor his favorite empress Mumtaz Mahal
Regarded as the pinnacle of Mughal architecture, blending Islamic, Persian, and Indian traditions
Adorned with intricate calligraphy, relief carvings, and pietra dura semi-precious stone inlay

facts_and_myths.claim: Shah Jahan ordered the hands of the master craftsmen amputated so they could never duplicate its beauty.
facts_and_myths.explanation: This gruesome story is a popular urban folklore myth without any contemporary historical backing; the chief architect went on to build Delhi's Red Fort.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The four flanking minarets were deliberately tilted slightly outward so that in the event of an earthquake, they would fall away from the central tomb.

facts_and_myths.claim: The marble exterior changes appearance and color throughout the day.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The high-grade Makrana marble naturally absorbs and reflects ambient daylight, appearing pinkish at dawn, pristine white at noon, and golden under the moon.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Over 1,000 elephants were used to transport rare construction materials from across India and Central Asia.

name: Statue of Liberty
visual_anchor: Heroic vertical 9:16 low-angle view of Lady Liberty lifting her gilded torch against the backdrop of the lower Manhattan skyline at golden hour.
core_traits: Colossal neoclassical copper sculpture on Liberty Island in New York Harbor, United States
Designed by French sculptor Frederic-Auguste Bartholdi with internal framework by Gustave Eiffel
Gift of friendship from the people of France to the United States dedicated in 1886
Holds a torch in her right hand and a tabula ansata inscribed with July 4, 1776 in Roman numerals

facts_and_myths.claim: The Statue of Liberty was originally constructed in its present green color.
facts_and_myths.explanation: She was originally the shiny reddish-brown color of a newly minted copper penny before natural oxidation created a protective green patina called verdigris.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The broken shackle and chain at her feet symbolize the abolition of slavery and liberation from oppression.

facts_and_myths.claim: Wind causes the Statue of Liberty to sway several inches during major storms.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Gustave Eiffel's flexible interior skeletal framework allows the statue to sway up to 3 inches and the torch up to 5 inches in high winds.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Her crown features seven spikes representing the seven seas and seven continents of the globe.

name: Machu Picchu
visual_anchor: Spectacular vertical 9:16 view of the stone agricultural terraces and granite ruins of Machu Picchu nestled beneath the iconic green peak of Huayna Picchu.
core_traits: 15th-century Inca citadel perched on an Andean mountain ridge 2,430 meters above sea level in Peru
Built as an imperial royal estate for Inca Emperor Pachacuti around 1450
Renowned for its dry-stone masonry where precision-cut blocks fit snugly without any mortar
Brought to global academic attention in 1911 by American explorer Hiram Bingham

facts_and_myths.claim: Machu Picchu was destroyed and sacked by Spanish conquistadors in the 16th century.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Spanish invaders never discovered Machu Picchu; it was gradually abandoned by the Incas and overgrown by cloud forest vegetation.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The site was engineered so skillfully that its sophisticated subterranean drainage systems prevent tropical landslides and erosion.

facts_and_myths.claim: Inca stonemasons fitted stones together so tightly that not even a knife blade can pass between them.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Using the technique called ashlar masonry, granite stones were carved and polished to interlock perfectly without mortar, allowing them to bounce and reset during earthquakes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: More than 60 percent of Machu Picchu's total construction lies underground in structural foundations and terraced drainage channels.

name: Sydney Opera House
visual_anchor: Gleaming vertical 9:16 view of the interlocking sail-like concrete shells of the Sydney Opera House jutting into Sydney Harbour waters at sunset.
core_traits: Multi-venue performing arts center situated at Bennelong Point in Sydney Harbour, Australia
Designed by Danish architect Jorn Utzon and formally opened by Queen Elizabeth II in 1973
World-famous for its dramatic vaulted white sail-like roof shells
One of the 20th century's most acclaimed architectural masterpieces and a UNESCO World Heritage site

facts_and_myths.claim: The iconic roof shells of the Sydney Opera House are completely pure white.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The roof is clad in over 1 million ceramic tiles in two distinct colors: glossy white and matte cream, creating an anti-glare textured finish.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Jorn Utzon solved the structural geometry problem of the roof by designing all the shells as segments cut from a single imaginary sphere.

facts_and_myths.claim: The construction of the Sydney Opera House finished years behind schedule and massively over budget.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Initially budgeted at 7 million Australian dollars and due in 1963, it ultimately cost 102 million dollars and opened a decade late in 1973.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Its air conditioning system cools the concert halls by drawing seawater directly from Sydney Harbour.

name: Big Ben
visual_anchor: Towering vertical 9:16 street perspective of the neo-Gothic Elizabeth Tower and illuminated clock face beside the Palace of Westminster along the River Thames.
core_traits: Iconic neo-Gothic clock tower situated at the north end of the Palace of Westminster in London, England
Commonly refers to the entire tower, though technically the nickname of the 13.7-ton Great Bell inside
Officially renamed the Elizabeth Tower in 2012 to commemorate the Diamond Jubilee of Queen Elizabeth II
Celebrated for its legendary punctuality and distinctive four-faced chiming mechanism

facts_and_myths.claim: Big Ben is the official legal name of the historic London clock tower.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The tower was originally called the Clock Tower before being renamed Elizabeth Tower in 2012; Big Ben is solely the nickname of the Great Bell inside.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Old British penny coins are placed onto the giant pendulum to fine-tune the clock's speed by fractions of a second.

facts_and_myths.claim: Big Ben kept chiming accurately even after being bombed during World War II.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Despite German Luftwaffe bombs damaging two clock faces and the palace roof during the Blitz, the clockwork mechanism continued chiming on time.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The minute hands on the four clock faces are each 4.2 meters (14 feet) long and made of copper sheet.

name: Christ the Redeemer
visual_anchor: Majestic vertical 9:16 drone shot of the colossal open-armed art deco statue atop Mount Corcovado overlooking Rio de Janeiro and Guanabara Bay.
core_traits: Colossal Art Deco statue of Jesus Christ crowning the summit of Mount Corcovado in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
Designed by French-Polish sculptor Paul Landowski and engineered by Heitor da Silva Costa
Depicts Christ with outstretched arms spanning 28 meters wide as a symbol of universal peace
Stands 30 meters tall atop an 8-meter pedestal, constructed of reinforced concrete faced with soapstone tiles

facts_and_myths.claim: Christ the Redeemer is repeatedly struck by lightning several times every year.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Due to its prominent mountain-peak position 700 meters above sea level, the statue is struck by lightning an average of three to six times annually.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In 2014, a violent lightning bolt chipped the fingertip of the statue's right hand just before the World Cup.

facts_and_myths.claim: The statue was transported and assembled in a single complete piece up the mountain.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It was shipped in individual modular sections and hauled up Mount Corcovado via a dedicated cog railway before being assembled on site.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Thousands of volunteers glued triangular soapstone tiles onto the statue, with many women writing personal prayers and names on the backs.

name: Petra
visual_anchor: Atmospheric vertical 9:16 view peeking through the narrow, towering rock cleft of the Siq canyon to reveal the sunlit rose-red facade of Al-Khazneh (The Treasury).
core_traits: Ancient archaeological city carved directly into vibrant pink sandstone cliff faces in southwestern Jordan
Flourishing capital of the Nabataean Kingdom dating back to the 4th century BC
Famous for its monumental rock-cut facade Al-Khazneh (The Treasury) and sophisticated water conduit systems
Nicknamed 'The Rose City' due to the distinctive red, pink, and ochre hues of its sandstone geology

facts_and_myths.claim: The monumental Treasury building in Petra actually housed vast hoards of royal gold.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Local Bedouin legends claimed Egyptian pharaohs hid treasure in the upper urn, but Al-Khazneh was actually a royal tomb and ceremonial mausoleum.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The giant urn at the top of the Treasury facade is pitted with bullet holes from Bedouin hunters attempting to crack it open.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Nabataeans built an ingenious desert hydraulic water system that supported 30,000 residents.
facts_and_myths.explanation: They engineered terra cotta piping, cisterns, dams, and aqueducts that harnessed seasonal flash floods into an artificial oasis.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Archaeologists estimate that over 80 percent of ancient Petra still lies buried unexcavated beneath desert sands.

name: Angkor Wat
visual_anchor: Vertical 9:16 silhouette of Angkor Wat's five lotus-bud sandstone towers rising above the lily-padded reflective moat under a vivid magenta and violet dawn.
core_traits: Vast sandstone temple complex situated in Siem Reap, Cambodia, surrounded by an expansive 190-meter-wide moat
Constructed in the early 12th century by Khmer King Suryavarman II as his state temple and eventual mausoleum
Originally dedicated to the Hindu deity Vishnu before gradually transitioning into a Theravada Buddhist site
Largest religious monument in the world by land area, covering over 162 hectares

facts_and_myths.claim: Angkor Wat was completely abandoned, forgotten, and swallowed by jungle vines until Western explorers stumbled upon it.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Cambodians never abandoned or forgot Angkor Wat; local Buddhist monks continuously inhabited and cared for the temple for centuries before French traveler Henri Mouhot visited.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Angkor Wat is prominently featured on the national flag of Cambodia, making it the only country flag centered on a specific religious building.

facts_and_myths.claim: Angkor Wat faces west, whereas most other Khmer temples face east towards the rising sun.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Facing west—the direction associated with death and the setting sun—strongly indicates that King Suryavarman II conceived it as a funerary monument.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Over 5 million tons of sandstone blocks were floated down the Siem Reap River on wooden rafts from Mount Kulen 40 kilometers away.

name: Chichen Itza
visual_anchor: Striking vertical 9:16 view of the step-pyramid El Castillo rising above the tropical Yucatan savanna under a brilliant blue sky.
core_traits: Major pre-Columbian Maya city and ceremonial center located on the Yucatan Peninsula in Mexico
Dominated by the 30-meter-tall step-pyramid known as El Castillo or the Temple of Kukulcan
Engineered with astonishing astronomical alignment honoring the feathered serpent god Kukulcan
Features Mesoamerica's largest ancient ball court, the Temple of the Warriors, and the Sacred Cenote

facts_and_myths.claim: During the spring and autumn equinoxes, shadows create the illusion of a giant slithering serpent.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The setting sun casts a series of triangular shadows along the north staircase that merge with a carved stone serpent head, mimicking a descending snake.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Clapping your hands at the base of El Castillo produces an echo that mimics the chirping call of the sacred quetzal bird.

facts_and_myths.claim: The entire ancient city of Chichen Itza was devoted strictly to human sacrifice and ritual warfare.
facts_and_myths.explanation: While religious rituals took place, Chichen Itza was primarily a thriving cosmopolitan trade metropolis, political capital, and hub for astronomy and mathematics.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Beneath El Castillo lies a massive subterranean water sinkhole called a cenote, which the Maya considered an entrance to the underworld.

name: Acropolis of Athens
visual_anchor: Dramatic vertical 9:16 golden-hour view of the marble columns of the Parthenon perched atop the limestone citadel overlooking the sprawling city of Athens.
core_traits: Ancient fortified citadel perched on a high rocky outcrop above the city of Athens, Greece
Contains the iconic Parthenon, the Erechtheion, the Propylaea, and the Temple of Athena Nike
Constructed during the Golden Age of Athens in the 5th century BC under the leadership of Pericles
Universal symbol of classical Greek civilization, philosophy, democracy, and Western architecture

facts_and_myths.claim: The columns of the Parthenon are perfectly straight and parallel vertical cylinders.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Architects Ictinus and Callicrates used optical illusions (entasis), curving horizontal beams and tapering columns slightly inward to appear straight from below.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The word 'Acropolis' comes from the Greek words 'akron' meaning highest point and 'polis' meaning city.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Parthenon was severely damaged in 1687 when a Venetian cannonball ignited stored Ottoman gunpowder.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Ottoman Turks used the ancient marble temple as an ammunition dump, which suffered a catastrophic explosion when besieged by Venetian forces.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Originally, the marble friezes and statues of the Acropolis were vividly painted in bright shades of blue, red, and gold.

name: Stonehenge
visual_anchor: Ethereal vertical 9:16 sunrise view of the massive sarsen trilithons and bluestones of Stonehenge standing in misty green Salisbury Plain fields.
core_traits: Prehistoric megalithic stone monument situated on Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire, England
Constructed in multiple distinct stages between roughly 3000 BC and 2000 BC
Consists of an outer ring of vertical sarsen standing stones topped by horizontal lintel stones
Aligned precisely with the direction of the sunrise on the summer solstice and sunset on the winter solstice

facts_and_myths.claim: Stonehenge was built by Celtic Druids as a pagan sacrificial altar.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Archaeological dating proves Stonehenge was built over a millennium before Celtic Druids ever existed in the British Isles.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The smaller volcanic 'bluestones' weighing up to 4 tons were transported over 150 miles (240 km) from the Preseli Hills in Wales.

facts_and_myths.claim: The stones are held together by sophisticated wooden-style woodworking joints.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Megalithic builders shaped the stone using ball-and-socket mortise-and-tenon joints and tongue-and-groove joints to lock horizontal lintels atop standing pillars.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Thousands of modern celebrants and tourists still gather at the stones each June to watch the summer solstice dawn align through the Heel Stone.

name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
visual_anchor: Playful vertical 9:16 perspective of the white marble freestanding bell tower tilting conspicuously on the emerald lawn of the Piazza dei Miracoli in Pisa.
core_traits: Freestanding Romanesque white marble bell tower situated in the Piazza dei Miracoli in Pisa, Italy
Began construction in 1173 and took nearly two centuries to finish due to frequent wars
Internationally famous for its unintended tilt caused by an unstable soft clay and sand foundation
Contains eight tiers of open marble arcades and houses seven functional bronze bells

facts_and_myths.claim: Galileo Galilei dropped two cannonballs of different masses from the top to disprove Aristotle's gravity theory.
facts_and_myths.explanation: While popularized by his biographer Vincenzo Viviani, most historians consider this an illustrative thought experiment rather than an actual physical event at the tower.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The tower began tilting as early as the construction of its third story in 1178, so builders made later floors curved slightly higher on one side.

facts_and_myths.claim: Engineering interventions in the late 1990s stopped the tower from collapsing and reduced its tilt.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Soil extraction beneath the higher north side successfully stabilized the foundation and reduced the lean by about 4 degrees, securing it for centuries.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Due to curved adjustments during historical construction, the tower is technically slightly curved like a banana rather than purely straight.

name: Mount Fuji
visual_anchor: Serene vertical 9:16 portrait of snow-capped Mount Fuji mirrored across Lake Kawaguchi, framed by blooming pink cherry blossom branches.
core_traits: Active stratovolcano and the highest mountain peak in Japan, standing 3,776 meters tall
Celebrated worldwide for its exceptionally symmetrical snow-capped volcanic cone
One of Japan's 'Three Holy Mountains' (Sanreizan) and a sacred pilgrimage site for Shinto and Buddhism
Immortalized in global art through Katsushika Hokusai's woodblock print series 'Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji'

facts_and_myths.claim: Mount Fuji is an extinct volcano that will never erupt again.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Geologists classify Mount Fuji as an active volcano with a low eruption risk; its last confirmed major eruption occurred in 1707 (the Hoei eruption).
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Mount Fuji is actually composed of three distinct overlapping volcanoes: Komitake, Ko-Fuji, and Shin-Fuji.

facts_and_myths.claim: Mount Fuji's summit is privately owned rather than state public land.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The peak above the eighth station belongs to Fujisan Hongu Seng Taisha, an ancient Shinto shrine that received formal ownership title centuries ago.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Over 300,000 people climb to the summit of Mount Fuji every year during the official summer climbing season.

name: Grand Canyon
visual_anchor: Breathtaking vertical 9:16 cliffside vista over the immense red, ochre, and purple stratified rock canyon walls carved by the Colorado River far below.
core_traits: Vast steep-sided river gorge carved by the Colorado River in northwestern Arizona, United States
Measures 446 kilometers (277 miles) long, up to 29 kilometers (18 miles) wide, and over a mile (1,800 meters) deep
Exposes nearly two billion years of Earth's geological history across colorful sedimentary rock strata
Designated a US National Park in 1919 and recognized as one of the Natural Wonders of the World

facts_and_myths.claim: The Grand Canyon is the deepest canyon in the entire world.
facts_and_myths.explanation: While among the most famous and scenic, deeper canyons exist, such as the Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon in Tibet and Cotahuasi Canyon in Peru.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Colorado River has taken an estimated 5 to 6 million years of continuous water flow to carve the gorge.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Grand Canyon creates its own localized microclimates and weather systems.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Due to extreme elevation differences between the high rim and low canyon floor, temperatures at the river can be 25 degrees Fahrenheit warmer than the rim.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Havasupai Native American tribe has lived inside the canyon for over 800 years and still receives mail delivered by mule train.

name: Niagara Falls
visual_anchor: Thundering vertical 9:16 shot of the massive curved curtain of turquoise water plunging into frothing white mist at Horseshoe Falls with a vibrant rainbow arc.
core_traits: Trio of massive waterfalls straddling the international border between Ontario, Canada, and New York, United States
Composed of Horseshoe Falls (the largest), American Falls, and the smaller Bridal Veil Falls
Drains Lake Erie into Lake Ontario along the Niagara River with the highest flow rate of any waterfall in North America
Major global tourist honeymoon attraction and premier source of hydroelectric power generation

facts_and_myths.claim: The flow of water over Niagara Falls completely froze solid into a stationary wall of ice.
facts_and_myths.explanation: While ice bridges and heavy surface freezing occur in sub-zero winters, the tremendous rushing water beneath the ice crust has never stopped flowing entirely.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: In 1969, the US Army Corps of Engineers completely diverted the American Falls dry for five months to clean the riverbed and study rock erosion.
